summary: An excerpt from Book 10 (part 160) of a novel in which a man visits a real estate broker's office to discuss selling his loft after a market downturn. The broker candidly explains the bubble-like market, estimates the loft will sell for about 1.8 million, and notes he has only about 200K equity, so he will likely break even or lose a point or two after fees and taxes. He reluctantly accepts the reality of his financial squeeze, and his thoughts turn to Ria, who never talked about money.
one_line: A man learns from a candid broker that his Manhattan-style loft will sell for about 1.8 million, leaving him near break-even.
key_facts: The broker estimates the loft will sell for about 1.8 million, a number she says she can deliver.
The man has only about 200K in equity in the loft.
The man expects to be down a point or two after paying fees and taxes.
The broker sold the apartment eight years ago to the family who owned it before the man.
The apartment came furnished, which the broker says is never nice stuff because nice is antithetical to corporate.
The broker says inoffensive is the best one can hope for in corporate furnishings.
The man came to the broker's office straight from Ate's door, taking the subway instead of cabbing it.
The man is on austerity measures effective immediately.
The broker offers to either walk him through the seven stages of grieving or list the loft at two or two point two million.
The broker says the market goes soft and everything falls down like a souffle after too much mortgage for too little home.
The man says he liked the broker because she read him perfectly.
The broker looks at the FOR SALE signs out the picture window while calculating the discount.
The man hates talking about money.
Ria never actually talked about money, only what money did.

entities.name: Ate
entities.role: person whose door the man came from before going to the broker's office

entities.name: Ria
entities.role: woman the man recalls who never talked about money
